section_1.title: Prerequisites & Intuition (1 min)
section_1.content: Briefly define a Normal Distribution N(μ, σ²) using the Bell Curve visual. Explain that adding two random variables is equivalent to calculating their convolution. Introduce the concept of independent variables.
section_1.example: Imagine two independent robots measuring the distance to a wall; each measurement has a 'blur' or error defined by a Bell Curve.

section_2.title: The Rule of Summation (1.5 min)
section_2.content: State the core theorem: If X ~ N(μ₁, σ₁²) and Y ~ N(μ₂, σ₂²), then X + Y ~ N(μ₁ + μ₂, σ₁² + σ₂²). Use an animation showing two shifting Bell Curves merging into a new, wider Bell Curve.
section_2.example: Robot A has error N(0, 1) and Robot B has error N(0, 2). The total combined error of the system is N(0, 1+2) = N(0, 3).

section_3.title: Visualizing the 'Why' (1.5 min)
section_3.content: Show the graphical superposition. Explain that the mean shifts by the sum of means (linear) and the variance spreads out by the sum of variances (Pythagorean-like addition of uncertainty).
section_3.example: Visual overlay: Two narrow spikes merging into one 'fatter' curve, representing how uncertainty accumulates when processes are stacked.

section_4.title: Real-world Application & Summary (1 min)
section_4.content: Apply the concept to a real scenario. Conclude that for independent Gaussian processes, the total output remains predictable and Gaussian. Emphasize that this simplifies complex systems into basic parameter arithmetic.
section_4.example: A package delivery process: Time to sort (N(10, 2)) + Time to drive (N(30, 5)) = Total time N(40, 7). The total distribution is still a smooth, predictable Bell Curve.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Map to right side of screen
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Rule of Summation", [
            "Adding two normal variables is a new normal.",
            "The mean of the sum is the sum of means.",
            "The variance of the sum is the sum of variances.",
            "The combined distribution is a new bell curve.",
            "This rule applies to all independent Gaussian distributions."
        ])

        # Colors
        COLOR_A = "#FF5733"
        COLOR_B = "#3357FF"
        COLOR_SUM = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
